name: The Three Elms of the Grote Kerk

location.address: Kerkplein 3, against the Grote Kerk, in front of theater De Vest

verified_sources: Gemeente Alkmaar, 'Lijst monumentale en waardevolle bomen in Alkmaar', March 2017 (openpdc.alkmaar.nl PDF), entry: Hollandse iep, Ulmus x hollandica, Kerkplein 3, standplaats plein, 1910-1920
access: Free. Public square (Kerkplein) beside the Grote Kerk and theater De Vest, in the historic city centre.
transport: Central Alkmaar, short walk from Alkmaar Centraal station
verify_notes: Three Dutch elms registered together as one monumental entry (register n_trees: 3), standing against the Grote Kerk (built 1470-1518, corroborated independently by Wikipedia) on the church square, in front of the De Vest theatre. LRMB's own site_history: 'De kerk is van het jaar 1500, gebouwd op een verhoogde zandrug. De drie iepen dateren van ongeveer 1920.' The 2017 municipal list independently records a Hollandse iep at the same address (Kerkplein 3) with a slightly earlier band, 1910-1920, versus LRMB's ~1920 estimate; likely the same registration rounded differently, note the small discrepancy rather than picking a winner. Sits about 150-280m from alk_004 (Elm of the Munnikenbolwerk) and alk_005 (Plane of the Clarissenbolwerk), part of the same walkable Bolwerken cluster. Register fields: owner_category gemeente, visitable ja, visible ja, setting plein (square). This is a compact, well-known ensemble with one obvious place to stand (the church square), not a scattered avenue. Dutch elm disease is active in the region (a different, unrelated elm on the Bolwerk near the historic ice cellar was felled in Jan 2019 for disease plus monument damage; see verify_notes pattern noted for other candidates), so a photo pass should check crown health, but no source suggests these three are affected.

name: The Weeping Silver Lime of Scheteldoekshaven
verified_sources: Gemeente Alkmaar, 'Lijst monumentale en waardevolle bomen in Alkmaar', March 2017 (openpdc.alkmaar.nl PDF), entry: Hangende zilverlinde, Tilia tomentosa Pendula, Bolwerk thv Scheteldoekshaven 5, 1930-1940
access: Free. Public park on the old city rampart (Bolwerk).
transport: Central Alkmaar, short walk from Alkmaar Centraal station
verify_notes: A weeping silver lime, Tilia tomentosa 'Pendula', a distinctive cascading form rather than an ordinary lime. Sits roughly 140-330m from alk_001, alk_004 and alk_005 in the same Bolwerken cluster. Register fields: owner_category gemeente, visitable ja, visible ja, setting park, form Treurvorm (weeping form).

name: The Relocated Yew of the Geestersingel

location.address: Roundabout (rotonde) on the Geestersingel; moved here 18 March 2018 from a courtyard behind Langestraat 115-117

verified_sources: Gemeente Alkmaar, 'Lijst monumentale en waardevolle bomen in Alkmaar', March 2017 (openpdc.alkmaar.nl PDF), entry: Venijnboom, Taxus baccata, Langestraat 115-117, 'staat in de winkel', age given as 150, criteria 'Omgevings- en locatiewaarde, zeldzaam' (rare) -- this predates the 2018 move and independently confirms the tree's original address and long-standing recognition

Pius Floris Boomverzorging, 'Video-impressie verplanten monumentale taxus in Alkmaar' (piusfloris.nl) -- the professional tree-moving company's own record that it relocated a monumental yew in Alkmaar, corroborating that the move described in the register genuinely took place (page content beyond the title could not be fetched this pass)
access: Free. Stands on a public roundabout, visible from the road at all times.
transport: Central Alkmaar, short walk from Alkmaar Centraal station
verify_notes: Remarkable relocation story, good material to lead the write-up with. The yew grew for well over a century in a courtyard behind a shop at Langestraat 115-117, hidden from view by surrounding buildings. When the building's renovation threatened the tree, the municipality spent four years preparing a transplant instead of felling it: on 1 April 2018 (register says work began 18 March 2018) it was lifted over the rooftops by a 450-tonne crane (Pius Floris Boomverzorging with Jos Blom kraanverhuur) and driven through the city to its new home on the Geestersingel roundabout, where the register says it has room to grow for '100 more years'. Two searches for independent news coverage of the move (Alkmaar Centraal / Streekstad Centraal, NHD) did not surface a directly fetchable article beyond the register's own account and the tree company's confirmation, per the two-attempts rule; not flagged as unverified given the pre-move municipal listing agrees independently on species, original address and age. The 2017 municipal list's age figure (150) is somewhat higher than LRMB's planting-band estimate (~130); both are vague/derived rather than a documented planting date, so the range is kept broad.

name: The Plane of the Munnikenbolwerk

location.address: Munnikenbolwerk, behind the Kunstuitleen (art lending library), Achter de Vest 3

verified_sources: Gemeente Alkmaar, 'Lijst monumentale en waardevolle bomen in Alkmaar', March 2017 (openpdc.alkmaar.nl PDF), entry: Plataan, Platanus x hispanica, 'Vest achter kunstuitleen 3', standplaats park, 1920-1930
access: Free. Public park on the old city rampart (Bolwerk).
transport: Central Alkmaar, short walk from Alkmaar Centraal station
verify_notes: Stands about 54 metres from alk_004 (The Elm of the Munnikenbolwerk, already published) on the same rampart. Register site_history: the planting date for this plane is dated fifty years later than the park's original 1870 landscaping by Zocher, i.e. it is not from the founding planting. NOTE FOR THE WRITER: keep this distinct from alk_005, 'The Plane of the Clarissenbolwerk', a different London Plane about 200-290m away at a different address (Zevenhuizen 23) with an earlier planted_band (1900-1910); the two are easily confused since both are London Planes on the same rampart system. Species recorded as 'Platanus x hispanica' in the municipal list, which is a synonym of Platanus x acerifolia (same species, different authority); mapped to the project's canonical London Plane per hard rule 9.

name: The Plume Elm of Molenbuurt

location.address: Behind cultureelcentrum De Vest, near Molenbuurt 25

verified_sources: Gemeente Alkmaar, 'Lijst monumentale en waardevolle bomen in Alkmaar', March 2017 (openpdc.alkmaar.nl PDF), entry: Pluimiep, Ulmus glabra Exoniensis, 'Bolwerk thv Molenbuurt 25', standplaats park, 1890-1900
access: Free. Public park (plantsoen) on the old city rampart (Bolwerk).
transport: Central Alkmaar, short walk from Alkmaar Centraal station
verify_notes: SPECIES DISCREPANCY, flagged rather than resolved silently: the LRMB register maps this tree generically to 'Dutch Elm (Ulmus x hollandica)', but the independent 2017 municipal list names the same tree, at the same address and planted in the same decade, as 'Pluimiep' / Ulmus glabra 'Exoniensis' (Exeter Elm, an upright, narrow-crowned cultivar of Wych Elm, called 'plume elm' in Dutch for its columnar shape). Same specimen beyond reasonable doubt (identical address 'Molenbuurt 25' and identical 1890-1900 planting band in both sources), but the two disagree on exactly which elm it is. Went with the municipal list's more specific naming since 'Pluimiep' is itself the LRMB register's OWN register_name for this exact entry (nr 1691012) even though its mapped 'species' field defaulted to the generic Dutch Elm bucket. Register site_history speculates it dates from the park's founding period (Zocher's 1870 conversion of the ramparts) though the planting band itself points to the 1890s. Stands about 70m from alk_004 and roughly 150-280m from the other Bolwerken candidates in this batch, same walkable cluster.

name: The Copper Beech of the Hertenkamp

location.address: East side of the Hertenkamp (deer park), Westerhoutpark / Alkmaarderhout

access: Free. Public city park (Alkmaarderhout), one of the oldest in the Netherlands, laid out from 1607.
transport: Central Alkmaar, roughly 15-20 minute walk or short bus ride from Alkmaar Centraal station
verify_notes: SINGLE DIRECT SOURCE: only the LRMB register names this specific tree; two searches (Dutch and English Wikipedia on Alkmaarderhout, a Historische Vereniging Alkmaar column on the park's trees) turned up general, independently-verified park history (founded 1607, largely redesigned by L.A. Springer around 1900-1903, Hertenkamp established 1902-1903) that is consistent with and supports the register's own site_history text, but neither names this beech specifically, so it is flagged rather than treated as fully corroborated. Register site_history: 'Deze rode beuk dateert vermoedelijk uit de Springerperiode' (probably dates from the Springer redesign period). IMPORTANT, checked carefully: there is a DIFFERENT copper beech, LRMB nr 1684912, only about 25-50 metres away near the park's music garden/flower clock (close to already-published alk_003), whose own register entry says it fell in Storm Poly on 5 July 2023 (confirmed independently: Storm Poly hit Alkmaar on that date, felling 500+ trees and severely damaging roughly 200 more per Rodi.nl and the municipality's own storm-damage recovery page) and now stands only as a stump to about 4 metres. This entry, nr 1688896, is the SEPARATE, still-standing beech on the east side of the Hertenkamp and should not be confused with the fallen one; no source suggests this one was affected by the storm. Register fields: owner_category gemeente, visitable ja, visible ja.
